chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the Quran is one, revealed from the Presence of One, but the differences come from the direction of the reporters.
ai.seo_question: Why are there differences in the Quran if it is from one God?
ai.summary: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Quran's divine essence is singular and unified, but textual variations stem from the human element of transmission (al-ruwah) rather than the revelation itself. This hadith is pivotal in Shia scholarship for distinguishing between the immutable divine word and the mutable nature of oral and written transmission, supporting the concept of multiple valid recitations (qira'at) without compromising the Quran's integrity.
